h1: Technical SEO Services — Fix the Issues Holding Your Rankings Back
intro: You can publish great content and still not rank — if your website has technical issues blocking Google from properly crawling, indexing, or trusting it. GrowZap's technical SEO services identify and fix the behind-the-scenes problems that quietly limit your search visibility, no matter how good your content is.
heroCta: Get a Free Technical SEO Audit

blocks.text: Technical SEO is the practice of optimizing your website's infrastructure — speed, structure, code, and crawlability — so search engines can access, understand, and rank your pages effectively. Unlike content or link-building, technical SEO is largely invisible to visitors, but it directly affects whether your other SEO efforts can work at all. Think of it as the foundation a house is built on: even excellent content and strong backlinks (the "house") won't perform well if the technical foundation underneath is unstable.

sections.heading: Common Technical SEO Issues We Find

subsections.title: Site Speed & Core Web Vitals
subsections.body: Slow-loading pages hurt both rankings and user experience. We identify what's slowing your site down — oversized images, unoptimized code, slow hosting — and fix it.

subsections.title: Mobile-Friendliness
subsections.body: Google primarily uses the mobile version of your site for ranking (mobile-first indexing). If your site doesn't function well on a phone, it directly impacts your rankings on every device.

subsections.title: Crawlability & Indexing Issues
subsections.body: If Google's crawlers can't access or properly index your pages — due to robots.txt errors, broken sitemaps, or blocked resources — those pages effectively don't exist in search, regardless of content quality.

subsections.title: Site Structure & Internal Linking
subsections.body: A clear, logical site structure helps both users and search engines understand how your pages relate to each other, and helps distribute ranking authority across your site.

subsections.title: Structured Data (Schema Markup)
subsections.body: Schema markup helps search engines understand the context of your content — and can unlock enhanced search features like star ratings, FAQs, and rich snippets directly in search results.

items.q: What's the difference between technical SEO and on-page SEO?
items.a: Technical SEO focuses on your website's infrastructure — speed, crawlability, structure — while on-page SEO focuses on individual page content, like titles, headings, and keyword optimization. Both are necessary; technical SEO ensures Google can access your content, while on-page SEO ensures Google understands it.

items.q: How do I know if my website has technical SEO issues?
items.a: Common signs include slow load times, pages missing from search results, crawl errors in Google Search Console, or rankings that don't match your content quality. A technical SEO audit will identify specific issues rather than relying on guesswork.

items.q: Will fixing technical SEO issues guarantee higher rankings?
items.a: No single fix guarantees a ranking increase, since Google's algorithm weighs many factors together. However, unresolved technical issues can actively prevent good content from ranking, so fixing them removes a ceiling on your potential performance.

items.q: Do I need technical SEO if my site is already getting traffic?
items.a: Possibly, yes. Even sites with decent traffic often have unresolved technical issues limiting further growth — an audit will show whether you're leaving performance on the table.

items.q: How often should technical SEO be reviewed?
items.a: We recommend a technical audit at least twice a year, or after any major website redesign, platform migration, or significant content addition, since these changes commonly introduce new technical issues.
